What I Cover Tsvetana Paraskova is an energy and commodities journalist who has contributed to Oilprice.com for nearly a decade, covering global energy markets, commodities,…

U.S. imports of Iraqi crude oil have slumped this year to a multi-decade low, EIA data show, as the Strait of Hormuz crisis has choked international shipments from OPEC’s second-largest oil producer.

U.S. imports have markedly dipped since March, to zero in several weeks this summer, after the closure of the Strait of Hormuz forced Iraq to slash its oil production.

articles.excerpt:

The shares had already faced significant volatility last week as concerns mounted over Big Tech's spending on AI infrastructure following the Democrats' sweeping victory in the US midterm elections.

articles.excerpt:

The Sensex ended at 81,106.65, up 107.25 points or 0.13 per cent, while the Nifty settled at 25,044.65, gaining 58.25 points or 0.23 per cent, after swinging between a high of 81,339.41 and a low of 80,519.31 on the Sensex through the day.

“After the sharp rally, some consolidation would be healthy for the market,” said Ajit Mishra, SVP, Research at Religare Broking, noting that foreign investors have pumped over $4.1 billion into Indian equities so far in November, providing a floor to any dip.

articles.title: US markets still reliant on tech stocks despite AI selloff and Democrat-win triggered political risks
articles.excerpt:
The US stock market is currently experiencing a significant pullback in technology and AI-related stocks. Investors are concerned that Democratic victories in the midterm elections may result in reduced data center spending. Despite recent declines, the technology sector remains dominant within the S&P 500 index. Upcoming technology earnings reports and the potential IPO of AI lab Anthropic are closely watched by investors.
